This is SFCC-91 Step 3 of 4: a new molecule, `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`, was just built. Test it and report findings — you never fix anything.

FILES IN THIS STEP (read them all in full first):
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts` (new)
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx` (new)

- `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` (edited — should be exactly a 2-line diff)

Also read the sibling atom it composes, `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx` (Step 2, already committed, do not touch), since this molecule's behaviour depends on it.

## What this component does

Renders a PDP colour-picker: a "Colour: Bay Blue" label row, and — when more than one colour variation has a populated index image — a row of `<ZimmColourSwatch>` children beneath it. It filters out unpopulated colours (AC 5), collapses to a label-only render when 0-1 colours remain after filtering (AC 1), and paginates in fixed 4-wide windows with prev/next chevron buttons when more than 4 populated colours exist (a Figma-mandated behaviour, not invented). Pagination is meant to move only the visible window, never the underlying selection.

## THE MOST IMPORTANT THING TO INVESTIGATE — a hypothesis, not a confirmed finding, verify it for real

Read `index.tsx`'s state carefully. `const [pageStart, setPageStart] = useState(0)` — the visible window always starts at position 0 on initial render/mount, regardless of where the actual `selectedValue` sits in the `populated` array. Separately, `isFocusable = isSelected || (!selectedValue && index === 0)`, computed per-item **within the currently rendered `windowed` slice only**.

Trace through this scenario by hand, then **write an actual test/render to confirm or refute it empirically** — do not just reason about it, prove it: a product has 6 populated colours, and `selectedValue` is set to the 6th one (i.e., a colour that would sit on the *second* page of a 4-per-page pagination, not the first). On initial render:
1. Does the component render page 1 (items 0-3) or does it render whichever page actually contains the selected colour?
2. If it renders page 1 (items 0-3): is there ANY item in that initial view with `aria-checked="true"`? (There shouldn't be, since none of items 0-3 equals `selectedValue`.) If no item shows as selected anywhere in the initially-visible page, is that a real, user-visible correctness defect — a shopper who lands on this PDP would see a colour swatch group where NOTHING appears selected, even though a colour genuinely is selected, just off-screen?
3. Separately: is there ANY item in that initial 0-3 window with `isFocusable=true` / `tabIndex={0}`? Walk the boolean logic yourself: `isSelected` is false for all of items 0-3 (the real selection is item 5), and `!selectedValue` is false (selectedValue IS set, just to something not in this window) — so `isFocusable` evaluates false for every rendered item on this page. If that's correct, is the entire visible radiogroup then untabbable via keyboard on initial page load (every child has `tabIndex={-1}`), even though a real, valid selection exists overall?

Build this exact scenario (render with 6 populated values, `selectedValue` = the 6th one's `value`) as a real test, run it, and report the ACTUAL observed behaviour — not your prediction of it. If this is confirmed, this is likely a 🔴 or at minimum a serious 🟡 finding: the correct behaviour would probably be to initialize `pageStart` to whichever page contains `selectedValue`, not always 0. If your test shows the component actually handles this correctly somehow (e.g. I've misread the logic), report that clearly too — don't let my hypothesis bias the result.

## Other things to test (fan out your own angles, but cover these)

- Run `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`, `npm run test`, `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` yourself — reproduce, don't trust the implementer's report. Baselines on this branch right now (after Steps 1-2): tsc 0 errors; test 27 files/417 tests before this step (you're adding one new test file — implementer reports 28 files/426 tests now, verify this yourself); lint 20 problems (4 errors pre-existing at routes.tsx:23,24 and recipeGuards.test.ts:116,335 — not this step's files)/16 warnings, exit 1; audit:tokens exactly 4 unacknowledged (none in this step's files)/22 acknowledged, exit 1.
- **AC 5 filter — verify it's keyed ONLY on `imageUrl`, not any other field.** This component's own prop type has no stock/orderability field at all (confirmed by reading `ZimmColourSwatchValue`) — good, that structurally prevents the base's `disabled={!orderable}` conflation the plan explicitly warned against. Confirm this by reading the type and the filter line directly.
- **AC 1 — filter-then-count.** Construct a case with 3 raw values where 2 lack `imageUrl` (so only 1 is populated) — confirm this renders the label-only branch (AC 1), NOT a 1-swatch radiogroup, and NOT a 3-swatch radiogroup. This is exactly the "filter first, then count" ordering the plan required — verify the actual code does this (filter happens before the `populated.length > 1` check), not just that the count happens to come out right by coincidence.
- **Pagination mechanics**: with 6 populated colours, confirm the "next" button advances to show items 4-5 (a 2-item final page, not items 4-7 which don't exist), confirm "previous" is disabled on page 1, confirm "next" is disabled on the final page, confirm clicking "next" then "previous" returns to the exact original 4 items in the same order.
- **Selection persistence across paging** — separately from the initial-mount hypothesis above: if a user is on page 1, no selection yet, then clicks "next" to page 2, does anything about the (still absent) selection state break? And if `selectedValue` matches an item that's currently on the visible page, does paging away and back preserve the correct `aria-checked` state on return (it should, since selection is derived from props, not local state)?
- **Truncation** — render with a very long colour name (e.g. 60+ characters) and confirm via computed style or DOM structure that the truncation CSS (`overflow: hidden; textOverflow: ellipsis; whiteSpace: nowrap`) is actually applied to the dynamic name element and NOT to the static "Colour:" text beside it. This was an explicit Figma design annotation ("If Label/Colour name is longer, use truncation") — confirm it's implemented, not just declared in a comment.
- **`ZimmIcon` usage** — confirm `type="chevron-left"`/`"chevron-right"` are real, valid values on `ZimmIconType` (read `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon/index.tsx` yourself) and that the icons actually render (or would, mocked) without throwing, given the known Vitest-throws-on-ZimmIcon gap this test file is supposed to work around via a mock — confirm the mock is present, correctly scoped, and actually prevents the throw (temporarily remove the mock and confirm the test file DOES throw/fail without it, then restore — this is the kind of "prove the workaround is real" check this project's standard expects).
- **Keyboard**: confirm arrow keys move DOM focus among the *currently rendered* (windowed) swatches only, wrapping at the ends, and do NOT change `selectedValue`/`aria-checked` anywhere (no `onVariationChange`-equivalent exists yet — arrows should be pure focus movement, nothing else). Confirm Up/Left move one way and Down/Right the other, matching base SFCC's own convention (check `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/swatch-group/index.jsx` for which direction is which, don't assume).
- **Recipe conformance**: confirm `parts: ['root','label','labelName','swatches','pagination','pageButton']` covers every key `index.tsx` reads via `styles.*` (recipeParts.test.ts should confirm this mechanically — verify it actually collected a case for this new recipe by name in its output, not just that the suite passed overall). Confirm zero raw hex/px/rem/em in the recipe file outside comments. Confirm no Chakra responsive-array shorthand anywhere (the plan explicitly forbids it — grep for array literals in style values).
- **No data-fetching hook** anywhere in `index.tsx` (grep for `useProduct`, `useCurrentBasket`, `commerce-sdk-react`, `useQuery`) — confirm this molecule remains a pure presentational leaf per this codebase's container/presentational rule.
- **Mutation check, done for real**: neuter the `values.filter((value) => Boolean(value.imageUrl))` line (make it a no-op returning `values` unfiltered), re-run the AC-5 test, confirm it actually fails, then restore and confirm it passes again. Report the real before/after output — implementer claims to have already done this and reports a specific failure message; reproduce it yourself independently rather than trusting the claim.
- **The label-group's own layout** (the direct-Chakra-props wrapper around "Colour:" + the name, described in index.tsx's own comment as having "no dedicated recipe part... per overrideStyling.md's 'your call' allowance") — read that section of `overrideStyling.md` yourself and judge whether this is a legitimate reading of that allowance or a rationalization for skipping a part that should exist. State your own judgement, don't just accept the comment's self-justification.

Report in the standard format: CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE/UNSUPPORTED, UNIFORM/ONE-OFF. State explicitly what you tried to falsify and could not, and what you could not verify at all (and why). Do not fix anything — only report. The pagination/initial-selection-visibility question above is the single most important thing in this report — do not bury it, lead with it.

1	import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
2	
3	/**
4	 * Recipe for the PDP colour-swatch group — the "Colour: Bay Blue" label row, and (when there is
5	 * more than one populated colour) the row of ZimmColourSwatch rectangles beneath it. This recipe
6	 * only lays the group out; each swatch's own fill/border/focus styling stays in the sibling
7	 * ZimmColourSwatch atom's own recipe.
8	 *
9	 * Values below are read directly off Figma for this exact component, not estimated — node
10	 * 40000307:13867 ("ColourOptions"), within Zimmermann_Design_System_2026.
11	 *
12	 * Six parts:
13	 *   - `root` — outer vertical flex container: the label row above, the swatches row below.
14	 *   - `label` — the label row ("labelContainer" in Figma): the label-group (the two
15	 *     "Colour:"/name text pieces — laid out via a plain Chakra-prop wrapper in the component
16	 *     itself, not a seventh part here; see index.tsx's own comment for why) plus the pagination
17	 *     controls, right-aligned purely via the label-group's own `flex: 1 0 0` rather than an
18	 *     absolute-position hack.
19	 *   - `labelName` — the dynamic colour-name text specifically (e.g. "Bay Blue"). Gets its own
20	 *     part, unlike the static "Colour:" piece beside it, because it alone carries the
21	 *     Figma-mandated truncation behaviour: "If Label/Colour name is longer, use truncation"
22	 *     (this node's own interaction annotation).
23	 *   - `swatches` — the horizontal row of rendered ZimmColourSwatch children.
24	 *   - `pagination` — wrapper around the two chevron buttons.
25	 *   - `pageButton` — each individual chevron button (24x24, holding a 16px ZimmIcon).
26	 */
27	export const ZimmColourSwatchGroup = {
28	  parts: ['root', 'label', 'labelName', 'swatches', 'pagination', 'pageButton'],
29	
30	  baseStyle: {
31	    root: {
32	      display: 'flex',
33	      flexDirection: 'column',
34	      // 8px between the label row and the swatches row. No background here — background lives
35	      // per-swatch, already handled by the atom's own recipe.
36	      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)',
37	    },
38	
39	    label: {
40	      display: 'flex',
41	      alignItems: 'center',
42	      // 24px. Matches spacing.xl exactly, so the named step is used rather than the numerically
43	      // identical --zimm-scale-600 alias — see bottomBar.css.ts's own `var(--zimm-scale-xl)`
44	      // usage for the same 24px value elsewhere in this codebase.
45	      height: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)',
46	      // 8px between the label-group and the pagination controls.
47	      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)',
48	    },
49	
50	    labelName: {
51	      textStyle: 'caption',
52	      color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)',
53	      // The truncating half of the label-group's two text pieces (the static "Colour:" text
54	      // beside it never truncates — see index.tsx). `flex: 1 0 0` lets it consume the
55	      // label-group's remaining width; `minWidth: 0` is required for a flex item to actually
56	      // shrink below its content size instead of overflowing; the rest is the standard
57	      // single-line-ellipsis triad.
58	      flex: '1 0 0',
59	      minWidth: 0,
60	      overflow: 'hidden',
61	      textOverflow: 'ellipsis',
62	      whiteSpace: 'nowrap',
63	    },
64	
65	    swatches: {
66	      display: 'flex',
67	      width: '100%',
68	      // Confirmed directly off the Figma export, not a stylistic default: the 4-swatch example
69	      // measures exactly 192px total width for four 48px-wide swatches (4 x 48, no gap
70	      // contribution) — swatches sit directly adjacent. Do not add a gap here; that would be a
71	      // real deviation from the design, not a stylistic default.
72	      gap: 0,
73	    },
74	
75	    pagination: {
76	      display: 'flex',
77	      alignItems: 'center',
78	      // No inter-button gap value exists in the Figma export handed to this step — left at the
79	      // flex default (no `gap` declared at all) rather than invented. Revisit if a designer
80	      // confirms a real value.
81	    },
82	
83	    pageButton: {
84	      display: 'flex',
85	      alignItems: 'center',
86	      justifyContent: 'center',
87	      width: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', // 24px
88	      height: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', // 24px
89	      // Resets the native <button> UA chrome so the box is exactly the 24x24 the design calls
90	      // for, with the 16px ZimmIcon centred inside it by the flex alignment above.
91	      padding: 0,
92	      border: 'none',
93	      background: 'none',
94	      cursor: 'pointer',
95	      // No confirmed Figma spec for a disabled visual treatment on this control — same "leave an
96	      // unspecified visual state alone rather than invent one" precedent as swatch-group's own
97	      // disabled colour logic (see this codebase's Known Gaps notes). The native `disabled`
98	      // attribute (set in index.tsx) already makes the control genuinely inert and announces as
99	      // disabled to assistive tech; only the cursor affordance is set here, which is a UX
100	      // keyword, not a design token.
101	      _disabled: {
102	        cursor: 'not-allowed',
103	      },
104	      // Same uniform ring every other interactive control in ui-kits/ uses (zimmColourSwatch,
105	      // zimmNavItem) — --zimm-focus-ring already composites the border-width/colour pair.
106	      _focusVisible: {
107	        outline: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring)',
108	        outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)',
109	      },
110	    },
111	  } satisfies Record<string, SystemStyleObject>,
112	};

} from 'app/components/icons';

// Figma iconography spec: node 1892:59595 — 34 of 34 types implemented.
export type ZimmIconType =
  | 'arrow-down'
  | 'arrow-link'
  | 'arrow-up'
  | 'bag'
  | 'bag-selected'
  | 'calendar'
  | 'carousel'

  // pending addition to the iconography spec in the next design sync.
  | 'phone'
  | 'whatsapp'
  | 'email';

export type ZimmIconSize = keyof typeof iconSizes;

type ZimmIconProps = {
  type: ZimmIconType;
  size?: ZimmIconSize;
  /** Pass Chakra token strings or CSS keywords (e.g. 'text.primary', 'currentColor').
   *  Do not pass hardcoded hex values — use theme tokens. */
  color?: string;
} & ({ 'aria-hidden': true; 'aria-label'?: never } | { 'aria-hidden'?: never; 'aria-label': string });

const ICON_MAP = {
  'arrow-down': ArrowDownIcon,
  'arrow-link': ArrowLinkIcon,
  'arrow-up': ArrowUpIcon,
  bag: BagIcon,
  'bag-selected': BagSelectedIcon,
  calendar: CalendarIcon,
  carousel: CarouselIcon,
  'carousel-selected': CarouselSelectedIcon,
  chat: ChatIcon,
  check: CheckIcon,
  'chevron-down': ChevronDownIcon,
  'chevron-left': ChevronLeftIcon,
  'chevron-right': ChevronRightIcon,
  'chevron-up': ChevronUpIcon,
  close: CloseIcon,
  delete: DeleteIcon,
  edit: EditIcon,
  'external-link': ExternalLinkIcon,
  info: InfoIcon,
  'info-selected': InfoSelectedIcon,
  location: LocationIcon,
  menu: MenuIcon,
  minus: MinusIcon,
  mute: MuteIcon,
  password: PasswordShowIcon,
  pause: PauseIcon,
  play: PlayIcon,
  plus: PlusIcon,
  profile: ProfileIcon,
  search: SearchIcon,
  share: ShareIcon,
  'share-2': ShareTwoIcon,
  wishlist: FavouritesIcon,
  'wishlist-selected': FavouritesSolidIcon,
  // Footer-specific custom icons — not yet in Figma node 1892:59595,
  // pending addition to the iconography spec in the next design sync.
  phone: PhoneIcon,
  whatsapp: WhatsAppIcon,
  email: EmailIcon,
} as const;

/** Atom — single icon from the Zimmermann icon set. Mirrors zimm-icon contract. */
export const ZimmIcon = ({ type, size = 'md', color = 'currentColor', ...aria }: ZimmIconProps) => {
  const Icon = ICON_MAP[type];
  // Both keys exist in every member of the union (one required, one optional-`never`), so the
  // rest object is indexable directly. The XOR is enforced by ZimmIconProps, not by a cast —
  // casting here only widened 'aria-hidden' from `true | undefined` to `boolean | undefined`.
  const ariaHidden = aria['aria-hidden'];
  const ariaLabel = aria['aria-label'];
  return (
    <Icon
      boxSize={iconSizes[size]}
      color={color}
      aria-hidden={ariaHidden}
      aria-label={ariaLabel}
      role={ariaLabel ? 'img' : undefined}
    />
  );
};
